title: Cap. X Arg. III: if reprobation hung on foreseen final impenitence/unbelief, no one would be reprobated except considered as dying — even as dead — because final perseverance/pertinacity is not fulfilled while we still live
pass_a_gloss: If the decree of reprobation hung from the foreseen final impenitence and unbelief of the reprobate, then no one would be reprobated except considered by God as dying, nay as dead. The reason is clear; Because while life is lived here, neither anyone's final perseverance in faith, nor final pertinacity in unbelief, is fulfilled. For whatever shall have been before the end is a step by which one ascends unto the summit, not a term by which the height's top is already held.
pass_b_english: Suppose the reprobation decree hung on the reprobates' foreseen final impenitence and unbelief. Then no one would be reprobated except as God considered him dying — nay, dead. Why is that plain? Because while life is lived here, neither anyone's final perseverance in faith, nor final pertinacity in unbelief, is fulfilled. Whatever comes before the end is only a step by which one climbs toward the summit, not the term by which the height's top is already held.
source_text: Si decretum reprobationis penderet ex praevisa finali impoenitentia et infidelitate reprobatorum, tum nemo reprobaretur nisi consideratus a Deo ut moribundus, imo ut mortuus. Ratio perspicua est; Quia dum hic vivitur, neque finalis cujusquam perseverantia in fide, neque finalis pertinacia in infidelitate adimpletur. Quicquid enim ante finem fuerit, gradus est quo ad fastigium ascenditur, non terminus quo jam culminis summa teneatur.
